- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The following classifications always require a petition.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The initial evidence listed below and the initial evidence listed under the instructions for a change of status or extension of stay must be included with a petition for a new or concurrent employment or for an extension where there is a change in previously approved employment.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] However, a petition for extension based on unchanged, previously approved employment should only be filed with the initial evidence required in the extension of stay instructions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] An E-2 CNMI investor is an alien who seeks to enter or remain in the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI) in order to maintain an investment in the CNMI that was approved by the CNMI government prior to November 28, 2009.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] An E-2 CNMI investor classification is specifically limited to an alien investor who has previously been granted a qualifying long term investor status under the laws of the CNMI.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] This classification allows an eligible alien to be lawfully present in the CNMI in order to maintain the investment during the transition period from CNMI to Federal immigration law.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] An investor’s nationality is not a qualifying factor in the issuance of an E-2 CNMI investor classification.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] This classification expires on December 31, 2029.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] A petition for the initial issuance of an E-2 CNMI investor classification must be filed within 2 years of the date the E-2 CNMI investor classification became available, which was January 18, 2011.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Petitions for the initial issuance of the E-2 CNMI filed after January 18, 2013 will be rejected.
